# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

### What it means if you rent GPUs

Until today, this autumn's rises were either quiet list adjustments caught after the fact (Verda's ten) or rises read on the day they landed. Lambda has done the renter-friendly thing — announced, dated and quantified, ten days ahead — and the size is the story: about 15% at once, on the three cards that anchor most training budgets. Anyone renewing or reserving Lambda capacity this month now has a hard date to plan around, and Nov 16 becomes a date this desk will verify first thing.

# Upcoming SaladCloud Price Changes: November 1, 2026

SaladCloud GPU pricing is changing on November 1, 2026: High, Medium, and Low Priority prices rise on 21 GPU classes. Lowest Priority is unchanged.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladCloud Mon Oct 26 2026

We're raising GPU prices on SaladCloud where demand has outpaced supply. High, Medium, and Low Priority prices are going up on 21 GPU classes. Lowest Priority pricing is unchanged on every class.

These changes take effect Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, and they will impact active and running instances at that time.

## Summary Copy Anchor Link

- High Priority prices are increasing on 21 GPU classes, by 10% to 20% on most of them.
- Medium and Low Priority prices are increasing on the same 21 classes, by smaller amounts.
- Lowest Priority pricing is unchanged on every GPU class.
- Every GPU class not listed below is unchanged at every priority level.

## Why prices are going up Copy Anchor Link

Over the past several weeks, demand has outpaced supply on many of our most popular GPUs. Several classes have been running almost entirely at High Priority, and many of you have waited for capacity or not gotten it at all.

SaladCloud runs on GPUs that individuals share with the network, and those providers have other options. Paying them a competitive rate is how we keep the machines we have and bring new ones online, so alongside these price changes we're raising provider payouts to attract more supply.

The increases are also weighted toward High Priority. When nearly everything runs at High, priority stops meaning much. High rises the most, Medium and Low rise less, and Lowest stays the same, so the gap between tiers widens: High stays available for work that needs it, and the lower tiers have more room.

If your workloads can tolerate preemption, Medium, Low, or Lowest Priority should become easier to get as more providers join. If you're not sure which priority fits a workload, reach out and we'll help.

results.title: RunPod Serverless GPU prices are up — B200 up about 25%, every tier higher | GPUJournal
highlights:
Nov 2, 2026

RunPod's Serverless GPU rates have risen on every tier, recorded between the Oct 26 and Nov 2, 2026 captures of its own pricing page: B200 $8.64 → $10.79 an hour is the largest move, up about 25%. RunPod announced nothing — the new figures are simply the ones live on runpod.io/pricing today, which we read first-hand on Nov 2.

Image: RunPod via runpod.io

What changed — the new figures read on RunPod's own pricing page (runpod.io/pricing) on Nov 2, 2026, against the figures captured from the same page on Oct 26, 2026: B300 $10.65 → $11.99 (up about 13%), B200 $8.64 → $10.79 (up about 25%), H200 $5.93 → $6.99 (up about 18%), H100 $4.79 → $5.39 (up about 13%), RTX 5090 $1.58 → $1.79 (up about 13%), RTX 4090 $1.10 → $1.34 (up about 22%), and the grouped L4 / A5000 / 3090 rate $0.69 → $0.75 (up about 9%). Every Serverless tier rose; none fell. On sourcing, plainly: the after-figures are RunPod's own page as we read it today; the before-figures are PricingSaaS Pulse's dated Oct 26 capture of that same page, because our own archive does not hold the October Serverless buckets — the comparison is recorded at pricingsaas.com/companies/runpod/diffs/2026W45. There is no RunPod announcement and no stated effective date; the honest date for the change is the window between the two captures.

...

What did not change: RunPod's Pods. Re-read on Nov 2, 2026, Pods Secure prices are exactly where they were — B300 $8.99, B200 $7.99, H200 $5.29, H100 SXM $3.99, A100 $1.79, L40S $1.09, RTX 5090 $1.19, RTX 4090 $0.89 and RTX PRO 6000 $2.49 an hour. Serverless is billed per second of worker time for inference endpoints, and its rates are not price-board rates, so the board does not move on this story — but anyone serving inference on RunPod Serverless is paying the new figures now.

What it costs: a Serverless worker that runs around the clock on a B200 now bills about $7,877 a month at $10.79 an hour, against about $6,307 at the old $8.64 — roughly $1,570 more per always-on GPU. An H100 worker running 24/7 goes from about $3,497 to about $3,935 a month. Serverless is normally bought for spiky traffic, where the per-second billing still beats an idle pod; the rises narrow that advantage at exactly the high end — B200 and H200 workers — where always-on endpoints are most common. This is RunPod's second rise in the recent record (Secure Cloud rose on Oct 14) and it extends the autumn pattern — Nebius on Oct 1, Verda eight times from Oct 23 to Nov 2, SaladCloud on Nov 1: rising prices are consistent with growing demand (our reading, labelled as interpretation; capacity and cost moves can also play a part).

results.title: KI-GPUs: B300-Mieten steigen um 106 Prozent, Token-Preise fallen
results.author: Rafael Müller
highlights:
Laut Berichten der Analysten Moses Sternstein und Alex Danco von der Risikokapitalgesellschaft a16z steigen die Mietpreise für Hochleistungs-Grafikprozessoren seit Mitte Juli spürbar an, während die durchschnittlichen Token-Preise zeitgleich um 58 Prozent eingebrochen sind.

## Schere zwischen Hardwarekosten und Token-Preisen

Nach Erhebungen von a16z verteuerten sich die Mietkosten für B300-Grafikprozessoren um 106 Prozent. Für B200-Systeme kletterten die Mietraten um 66 Prozent, während für Modelle der H100-Reihe ein Anstieg von 17 Prozent gemessen wurde.

Nach den am 30. Oktober 2026 von a16z veröffentlichten Auswertungen sind die durchschnittlichen Token-Preise seit Mai um 67 Prozent gefallen, wohingegen die Ausgaben für Token um 120 Prozent zulegten.

...

## Spotmärkte und

...

Auf den Handelsplätzen spitzt sich die Lage bei kurzfristig verfügbarer Rechenleistung zu. Für Nvidia-B200-Einheiten stiegen die On-Demand-Mietpreise in der vergangenen Handelswoche um 12,9 Prozent auf einen Höchststand von 8,54 US-Dollar pro GPU-Stunde auf der Ornn Exchange. Beim Anbieter Nebius haben sich die Spotpreise für identische B200-Hardware in den letzten sieben Tagen mehr als verdreifacht.

Das Unternehmen hatte die On-Demand-Preise zum 1. Oktober 2026 bereits breitflächig angehoben: für B300-Chips um 21 Prozent von 7,85 auf 9,50 US-Dollar pro Stunde, für B200 um 20 Prozent, für H200 um 19 Prozent sowie für H100 um 17 Prozent.

Auf Unternehmensseite sorgt die Preisdynamik für Verwerfungen. Die Aktie des Cloud-Anbieters CoreWeave verzeichnete in derselben Woche ein Minus von 25,2 Prozent. Bei dem Unternehmen entfielen 98 Prozent der Umsätze im zweiten Quartal auf Festpreisverträge, während ein Auftragsbestand von 104 Milliarden US-Dollar größtenteils erst nach Mitte 2028 umsatzwirksam wird.

Citadel-Analyst Frank Flight erläuterte, dass die Terminpreise für Nvidia H100 trotz niedrigerer Raten bei längeren Laufzeiten stabil bleiben, was die Preissetzungsmacht der Anbieter knapper Kapazitäten unterstreiche. Social Capital bezifferte den Preisanstieg bei H100-Mieten seit Dezember auf 45 Prozent.

...

Angesichts der Volatilität etablieren sich neue Finanzderivate. Die CME Group hat Futures auf die Mietkosten von Nvidias H100 und B200 beantragt; die behördliche Prüfung wurde bis zum 9. November verlängert.

results.title: Verda raises prices for the ninth time — all nine GPUs up about 1% again | GPUJournal
highlights:
Nov 4, 2026

Read on Verda's own pricing page today, Nov 4, 2026, against the figures read there on Nov 3: every GPU in Verda's range rose by about 1% — GB300, B300, B200, H200, H100, both A100s, the RTX PRO 6000 and the L40S. One flat day, then the rise run resumed.

The pattern: Verda rose on Oct 23, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30, held on Oct 31 and Nov 1, rose an eighth time on Nov 2, held on Nov 3 — and has now risen a ninth time. Its GB300, the only GB300 rate we list, has gone from $11.82 an hour at our Oct 19 check to $13.31 today, up 12.6% in just over two weeks. Verda is not alone in the pattern: Nebius raised across the board on Oct 1, RunPod Secure on Oct 14, SaladCloud's Priority rise took effect Nov 1 and RunPod Serverless rose by Nov 2. ...

Nine rises in thirteen days is no longer noise — it is one provider repricing steadily upward while the market's best verified offers stay put.

results.title: AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at
results.author: Paul Nugent
highlights:
# AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at

Paul Nugent

Nov 4, 2026

AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

The critical detail: Trainium pricing is unchanged.

AWS now operates two parallel compute economics tracks:

🔹 NVIDIA TRACK: +20% — you absorb Nvidia's pricing power, supply constraints, AND AWS's margin protection layered on top.

🔹 TRAINIUM TRACK: flat — Amazon subsidizes the economics because every workload that migrates to Trainium deepens lock-in to the AWS ecosystem.

results.title: Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU: what capacity costs | Casitel
highlights:
Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU rates for the H100, H200 and B200, read on 3 November 2026, with published commitment discounts and what else changes the bill.

...

A neocloud is a cloud built around GPUs. Newcomer, writing in May 2026, names Lambda and Crusoe as neoclouds that own their chips and sell the compute. CoreWeave and Nebius are two more. Regional ones sit in other markets: E2E Networks in India and Sakura Internet in Japan both publish GPU rates and commitment terms.

The other side is the hyperscalers: Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle. They sell GPUs as one product inside a much larger cloud.

## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

## What commitments change

Every provider here says a commitment lowers the rate. Few publish by how much.

C Compute · published commitment discounts Read 3 Nov 2026

E2E Networks 10% to 30%, its own figure

Sakura Internet 5% for 6 months, 10% for 12

Each provider's own pages, read 3 Nov 2026. Discounts off list rates.

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.
- Google Cloud lists Flexible Savings Plan rates on the Vertex AI page. For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025. Those are cuts from its earlier prices, not discounts off today's rate.
- Nebius and Lambda name no percentage. Both point large buyers to sales.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Median on-demand prices for B300, B200, H200, H100, MI300X and more across specialist GPU clouds, converted to monthly cost, with how prices moved this year.

- November 4, 2026
- 7 min read
- By the CoreGPU team

Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
